findings.summary: parse_block only decodes syntax and returns whatever function name the model wrote (parsers.py), and nothing here checks it against the offered tools, so a call to an unoffered function, or under a named choice to a different function, reaches the client as an executable tool call.
requires_call is true only for required, so a named tool_choice accepts a plain-text answer with no call and, on a tokenizer without a tool format, falls through to tools-ignored instead of 400.

The streaming branch validates tools but never resolves tool_choice, so a streaming request with required or a named function streams text with 200 instead of the promised 400 (and an unknown named function is not rejected either).
